newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end 1.71 pct lower on Telkom.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end 1.71 pct lower on Telkom.

text.p: Jakarta share prices closed sharply lower on Tuesday, with heavy foreign selling in utility giant Telkom depressing other counters, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 11.50 points, or 1.71 percent, to close at 659.44 points. In broader market sentiment, losers led gainers 100 to 37, with 42 issues unchanged.

Telkom was the most actively traded counter, with volume exceeding 44 million shares. It fell 175 rupiah to 3,650 rupiah on what brokers said was the emergence of a possible competitor in the shape of a consortium that includes tycoon Sudwikatmono, a brother-in-law of President Suharto.
"There was heavy selling in Telkom, especially by foreign investors on speculation it might face a competitor," one broker said. "The Telkom selling affected other counters."
Securities analysts said Telkom was expected to remain under pressure on continued speculation that the blue-chip company might lose its monopolyof basic telecommunication services.

Brokers said the speculation put a positive spin on conglomerate Bimantara, which rose 200 rupiah to an intra-day high of 3,325 rupiah before closing at 3,225 rupiah on profit taking. They said there was market talk that Telkom's possible rival might use Bimantara as its vehicle.
"Talk is that Bimantara might be the vehicle for the Telkom competitor," one broker said. Bimantara is controlled by President Suharto's second son Bambang Trihatmodjo.

Brokers said banking stocks remained under pressure due to the general weak market sentiment, and speculation on whether the central bank would take action against banks that breached the recently-announced limits on credit growth.

"Is the central bank going to take action against banks that breach the limit? That seems to be on many people's minds, but I personally don't think so," an analyst said, adding that some investors were possibly taking profits in banking stocks.
First-tier Bank Negara Indonesia fell 25 rupiah to close at 1,375 rupiah on a volume of 17.6 million shares, making it the second most active counter after Telkom.

Blue-chip Bank International Indonesia was down 25 rupiah to 1,800 rupiah, with 5.3 million shares changing hands, while secondliner Bank Pikko lost 200 rupiah to end at 1,075 rupiah on a volume of 10.5 million shares.
Brokers said they expected the market to stay soft on Wednesday as there were no fresh funds entering the country, while local players were downsizing their investments.
